idiom_name: discriminated-union Action + pure reducer(state, action) + typed dispatch/useReducer
implementation_notes: A discriminated union of action types plus a pure reducer(state, action: Action): State is TypeScript's direct expression of the intent-reduce-state loop: the compiler checks that each action carries its payload and that the switch stays exhaustive (never-check), React's useReducer with a typed dispatch drives a component, and a typed store (Redux Toolkit slices, or an RxJS scan/BehaviorSubject pipeline) covers non-React views. What replaces the MVI classes is the action union plus the reducer function, with effects outside the reducer - which is why the classification is idiomatic; what remains the developer's job is immutable updates, because no type checks that only the reducer creates state.
pitfalls: Casting actions (as Action) or typing state as any erases the narrowing that makes the reducer safe; keep discriminated unions and never-checks.
An optional field typed string | undefined can silently differ between branches and break equality-based change detection; build whole states under strict mode.
Redux Toolkit Immer drafts must not leak: returning a draft from a selector exposes non-serializable proxies and defeats devtools/time travel.
Splitting the action union across files loses exhaustiveness; keep one Action union per feature (or compose unions) so the switch stays total.
